 Having a defibrillator close at hand can make the difference between life and death for someone experiencing life-threatening arrhythmia. The medical device administers an electric shock to essentially restart one’s heart rhythm when it goes off the rails, thus preventing cardiac arrest and potentially saving that person’s life. There are multiple types of defibrillators out there, but the one we’ll focus on today is called an automated external defibrillator (AED).

 CarBuzz recently found a patent filed by Jaguar Land Rover to the UK Intellectual Property Office, showing an AED compatible with an electric or hybrid vehicle. So, let’s dive straight into the deep end and see what JLR’s invention is all about, because it could definitely have a positive impact if the idea is eventually put into practice.
 JLR’s Tech Could Turn EVs And Hybrids Into Genuine Lifesavers
 Jaguar Land Rover defibrillator patent drawing UK Intellectual Property Office 
 Based on the patent’s description, the company would hypothetically build an automated external defibrillator that can be plugged straight into a hybrid or fully-electric car . An external high-voltage input port is designed to draw 200 volts (or more) from the vehicle’s electrical system. From there, the device would function just like a typical AED.
 There is an output port where the electrodes would be connected, and audio instructions on how the defibrillator should be used are provided via a speaker. Additionally, we also see a small user interface allowing the operator to control the electrical charge transmitted through the device. And, of course, the AED would have to be light and compact so users could handle and transport it with ease.
 What Would JLR Be Accomplishing With This?
 Jaguar Land Rover HQ building logo 2025 Jaguar Land Rover 
 Of course, portable AEDs have been around for quite some time now, even if they’re not as readily available as they should be. The ingenuity of JLR’s patent lies in the fact that its module would work with hybrids and EVs, perhaps beyond the models in its own lineup. This could solve the scarcity problem at least in part, but it can also make a massive difference if adopted on a large scale.
 Think about it; electrification is becoming increasingly common in one form or another, so devices like the one patented by Jaguar Land Rover could save countless lives as they become widespread. And although we’re still a long way from that scenario if it even materializes at all, it’s good to know the technology may one day be widely available.
 CarBuzz Insight – Why This Matters:
 With this sort of tech becoming a reality, our everyday vehicles would be so much more than a means of transportation. They could potentially save someone’s life at a moment’s notice, and this definitely sounds like a good enough reason to make these car-compatible AEDs a real thing.
 Inventions made for our convenience or a better driving experience are cool and all, but JLR is really thinking outside the box here. Perhaps we will eventually look back at its idea and feel thankful for it keeping many people alive in what could have otherwise been a life-ending predicament.
 Patent filings do not guarantee the use of such technology in future vehicles and are often used exclusively as a means of protecting intellectual property. Such a filing cannot be construed as confirmation of production intent.
 Source: UK Intellectual Property Office
